task:
Implement issue #537: contain the code defect that allowed a supposedly non-secret retained-V3 recovery artifact to include literal database credentials. Start from current origin/main at fd64ef8e14b5b026cec2d14949115ab681fb0b7d. Read CLAUDE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/development/chatgpt-ops-control-plane.md, docs/operations/github-actions-hetzner-operator.md, scripts/operator/README.md, scripts/operator/recover_v3_runtime_contract.py, scripts/operator/ed_new_ops.py, .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml, and all tests covering the recovery/operator path. Keep scope to the read-only recovery helper, its workflow/upload contract, documentation, and focused tests. Do not access the remote host, download or inspect artifact 9773572090, print or guess any credential, rotate credentials, delete Actions artifacts, deploy, touch production, modify databases, change DNS, start/stop retained containers, implement #527, or change Stage 27/runtime/product/data/CRE/CPE/Journal behavior. The wrapper will commit and push an isolated branch; do not commit, push, merge, or deploy yourself.

Proven root cause and safety facts (values deliberately omitted): the 2026-08-31 recovery run selected 407 files by filename/suffix only. The archive manifest matched every byte, but selected historical scripts and artifacts included the same literal non-placeholder PostgreSQL password in credentialed URIs. `artifacts/v3/phase-4c/final/container-inspect-start.json` also included Docker `Env` values containing `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and a credentialed `DATABASE_URL`. The existing receipt field `docker_inspect_env: false` described only the helper's live Docker query and falsely suggested that no environment material could exist inside selected source files. No raw value may enter source, tests, logs, fixtures, documentation, or the final summary.

Required design: secrets are not runtime authority. Produce a deterministic, review-safe recovery archive only after a complete bounded content preflight. Use a two-pass or equivalent design so no archive byte is emitted until every selected file has been read, classified, and made safe. Keep the existing path traversal, symlink, regular-file, required-Compose-config, file-count, per-file and total-size bounds, read-only Docker-label lookup, no DB access, no host mutation, and deterministic tar metadata. Bump the recovery schema because the manifest contract changes.

For every selected source file, record original path, mode, size and SHA-256. The archive may contain either: (a) the original bytes when verified safe; (b) a deterministic sanitized copy when high-confidence secret material can be removed without ambiguity; or (c) no copy when the file must be excluded. The manifest must explicitly record a disposition (`verbatim`, `redacted`, or `excluded`), reason codes with no secret values, original identity, and archive identity when present. Required Compose config files may not disappear silently; safe templates/placeholders should remain verbatim, and a config requiring redaction must remain syntactically usable/reviewable or the operation must fail closed.

Content safety coverage must include, at minimum: PEM/private-key blocks; recognised GitHub/OpenAI/AWS-style token/key formats; credentialed PostgreSQL and Redis URIs; literal sensitive assignments such as `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...`; JSON/Docker-inspect structures containing `Env` or environment mappings with sensitive names or credentialed URI values; and nested strings containing those patterns. Treat explicit template/sentinel forms such as shell variable expansion, GitHub expressions, Jinja-style placeholders, angle-bracket placeholders, and `REDACTED`/`CHANGEME`-style sentinels as non-secret templates, with focused tests preventing needless false positives. Do not treat ordinary mentions of words like password/token/key in prose or source identifiers as secrets. If content is binary/invalid for the allowed text suffix, contains an unsafe construct that cannot be deterministically sanitized, exceeds the preflight memory/size contract, or sanitization would leave invalid JSON where JSON structure is being preserved, fail before emitting output. Never echo a matched value or include it in an exception.

For JSON environment captures, parse and recursively sanitize rather than regex-corrupting JSON. Preserve valid JSON and deterministic formatting. Replace sensitive values with a fixed sentinel, and redact credential components inside URI strings. For ordinary UTF-8 text, use narrowly defined high-confidence transformations and then re-scan the transformed bytes. Private-key blocks and unrecognised token/key material should be excluded or cause a fail-closed stop; choose and document one consistent contract. After transformation, run a final high-confidence scan over every would-be archive payload. The receipt must state counts for verbatim/redacted/excluded files and accurately distinguish live Docker metadata fields queried from environment-bearing source files found and sanitized/excluded.

Workflow/upload contract: verify that a helper failure cannot upload a partial or stale archive. If the current shell pipeline or temp-file handling leaves a stale-file risk, fix it with a unique temporary path, cleanup trap, checksum after successful helper completion, and upload only on success. Do not weaken SSH host pinning or any operator allowlist.

Tests: extend the existing recovery tests with synthetic values only. Include fixtures for (1) a safe templated Compose file that remains verbatim; (2) a shell/Python text file with a synthetic credentialed URI that becomes redacted with original and sanitized hashes recorded; (3) a Docker-inspect-style JSON `Env` list with synthetic `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL` values that remains valid JSON and contains only the fixed sentinel; (4) a private-key/token fixture that is excluded or fails according to the documented contract; (5) comments/prose/source identifiers mentioning password/token/key that remain safe; (6) final re-scan and no matched value in manifest/receipt/errors; (7) no output bytes on any preflight failure; (8) manifest totals/counts/hashes/dispositions and deterministic archive bytes; (9) existing symlink/traversal/required-config/size limits; and (10) workflow no-stale/no-partial upload structure. Add/update another contract test only if genuinely needed; do not weaken unrelated coverage.

Documentation: explain that the 2026-08-31 artifact was structurally intact but unsafe and is not authority, that its deletion and credential active-use/rotation disposition are separate owner containment actions tracked in #537, and that a successful workflow status alone does not prove a recovery artifact is safe. Do not put a raw value or downloadable artifact link in docs. Keep #527 explicitly blocked until a fresh safe artifact is independently verified.

Validation: install only the existing pinned tests/requirements-ci.txt into the worker `.venv` if necessary. Run the focused recovery/operator/workflow tests, tests/test_ci_stall_detection.py, relevant repo-hygiene tests, `python -m ruff check` on changed Python files, parse all changed workflow YAML with pinned PyYAML, and `git diff --check`. Also create an in-memory synthetic archive and independently assert no high-confidence secret pattern remains in any member. End with exact changed files, exact tests/results, the chosen redaction/exclusion contract, and limitations (including that artifact deletion/credential rotation and a real recovery rerun were not performed).
